past_paper_mcqs.stem_text: If a loading truck has an output of 3600 J and its efficiency is 50%, then the input provided to the truck will be
past_paper_mcqs.explanation: Efficiency = $(\text{Output Energy} / \text{Input Energy}) \times 100$. Rearranging for Input Energy: $\text{Input} = (\text{Output} / \text{Efficiency}) \times 100 = (3600 / 50) \times 100 = 7200\text{ J}$.

past_paper_mcqs.stem_text: The kinetic energy of a 0.5 kg bullet moving with velocity of 500 m/s is
past_paper_mcqs.explanation: Kinetic Energy ($KE$) = $\frac{1}{2} m v^2 = \frac{1}{2} \times 0.5\text{ kg} \times (500\text{ m/s})^2 = 0.25 \times 250000 = 62500\text{ J}$.

crqs.question: Explain why upthrust acts in the upward direction on an object immersed in a fluid.
crqs.answer: Hydrostatic pressure in a fluid increases with depth (P = ρgh). Consequently, the upward pressure on the bottom surface of an immersed object is greater than the downward pressure on its top surface, producing a net upward buoyant force (upthrust).
crqs.source: AKU-EB SSC-I Model Paper II Q.7(b)(ii)

erqs.question: i. Explain why the walls of a dam filled with water are usually wedge-shaped. ii. If the density of water is 1,000 kg/m³, calculate the depth of water in a dam when the pressure at the bottom is 100,000 Pa (g = 9.8 m/s²).
erqs.answer: i. Liquid pressure increases with depth (P = ρgh), so water exerts a much larger lateral force near the bottom of the reservoir; a wider wedge-shaped base provides the structural strength to withstand this pressure. ii. Using P = ρgh: h = 100,000 / (1000 × 9.8) = 10.2 m.
erqs.source: AKU-EB SSC-I 2025 Annual Paper II Q.7(b)
